draft.title: Aboriginal spiritualities and dispossession
card: For Aboriginal peoples, land is not just a place to live. It holds the Dreaming, the stories and laws that come from the ancestral beings and shape life, and people have a duty to care for their Country.
Kinship ties people to each other and to Country. Ceremony is carried out on particular land and keeps the Dreaming and these ties alive.
Dispossession means being removed from land. When people were moved off Country, they could lose access to sacred sites and ceremony, and their connection to the Dreaming and kinship was damaged.
The Stolen Generations were Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children removed from their families by governments and missions. Many lost contact with family, Country, language and ceremony.
draft.remember: Separation from land cut links with the Dreaming, kinship and ceremony, because for Aboriginal peoples these are bound up with Country.

a.q: Why did removal from Country damage Aboriginal spiritual life?
opts: Dreaming, kinship and ceremony are tied to particular land
Aboriginal spirituality has no beliefs outside of ceremonies
Spiritual life depended on owning land under European law
Only the elders had spiritual ties to land, and they stayed
a.why: Because the Dreaming, kinship and ceremony are tied to particular Country, being removed from it cut those links. Legal ownership is not the reason: the connection is spiritual and does not depend on European law.
a.clue: Think about what Country holds for Aboriginal peoples.

b.q: Jarrah was taken from his family as a child and raised far from his Country. Which is the most likely effect on his spiritual life?
opts: He lost contact with the ceremony and kinship tied to Country
He lost his Dreaming, which cannot exist away from his family
He gained a stronger link to Country in his new surroundings
He was unaffected, because the Dreaming is only old stories
b.why: Removal from family and Country separated him from the ceremony and kinship that keep the Dreaming alive. It is too strong to say the Dreaming was destroyed, as the card says the connection was damaged and cut, not that it ceased to exist.
b.clue: Look at what ceremony and kinship depend on.
